precepts.text: Now if you know you got to serve this man for food, water, and clothing, you can't go I hate your guts, I just want to. You think you're going to have a job? You're going to lose everything.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”. Use this verse to your advantage; don't run from it. In Romans 9:13 Paul speaks on behalf of God, and that is what God says about Esau. But God's law to us is: thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother, a wicked brother.

And look at our condition: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. If you know you have to serve this man for food, water and clothing, you can't go around saying I hate your guts, I just want to harm you. You think you're going to have a job? You're going to lose everything.

There was a brother at camp on Eastern Parkway, on medication, who said he couldn't work because he gets violent: I hate white people; when I sit in the office or do construction, I look at them and I just want to harm them. And there was a martial artist, a black belt, who drew young Haitian brothers to him, skinny at first and diesel two or three months later, calling themselves the barbershop crew in Brooklyn. One night a brother called to be gotten out of jail: they were getting diesel and learning to fight to do home invasions and burglaries.

The bottom line is, professing yourself to be an Israelite is not on the premise of wanting to harm white people. A lot of Israelite camps teach that, and the leaders of those camps are bums: either they are bums or they live off the congregation, and they can talk that way without repercussions because they have no boss to answer to. We serve our enemies under the curse, so we keep the law: we do not abhor the Edomite.

precepts.text: I did an interview with Soft White Underbelly. He said, when you're teaching this, doesn't it cause people to be angry? Yes, they get angry. The Bible says anger is okay: be ye angry, and sin not. The sin would be if you start murdering people; the sin would be you start stealing.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
In an interview with Soft White Underbelly came the question: when you're teaching this, doesn't it cause people to be angry? Yes, they get angry. The Bible says anger is okay: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath”.

The sin would be if you start murdering people; the sin would be if you start stealing. Remember the series American Gods: Anansi was on a slave ship and asked, are you angry? That's good; anger gets stuff done. Surely oppression makes a wise man mad. Not I'm going to go kill everybody, but let's organize, let's do better. And you know who got that actor fired? Black people, who said what he was saying would make white people mad. The whole show was cancelled, and all those black people lost their jobs.

So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” does not mean you can't be angry at what was done. Be angry and sin not: let the anger drive you to organize and build, not to harm, steal or kill.

precepts.text: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. That's if possible. We've seen some instances on the news where it was impossible; you had to throw hands to some people, because some people are irate, some people are unreasonable.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” That's if possible. As much as lies in you, you live peaceably, and that includes the Edomite the law says you shall not abhor, for he is thy brother.

But we've seen some instances on the news where it was impossible; you had to throw hands with some people, because some people are irate and some people are unreasonable. Paul did not say peace at any cost; he said as much as lieth in you.

So the law of Deuteronomy 23:7 is not a command to be harmless. It is a command not to carry hatred and seek harm. We live peaceably as far as it depends on us, and we are not the ones who start it.

precepts.text: The key is without a cause. Meaning if I'm mad with you and I have no reason to be mad with you, I'm in danger of judgment. But now somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one; do you have a reason? Yes. The dude said, in order to be a man of peace, you must be capable of great violence. If you're not capable of violence, you're just harmless.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”. The key is without a cause. If I'm mad with you and I have no reason to be mad with you, I'm in danger of judgment.

But now somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one: do you have a reason? Yes. At one of the schools a sister's phone kept going ding, somebody sending her indecent pictures on Instagram. It went on for a while until the heads of the school had everybody bring their phones up and closed the doors. One brother said his phone was dead; they said don't worry, we got a charger. Sure enough, it was him. They told everybody to move back, and the husband said, move out my way. That is anger with a cause.

As the saying goes, in order to be a man of peace you must be capable of great violence; if you're not capable of violence, you're just harmless. So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” forbids hatred without a cause, not the defense of your own.

precepts.text: There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel; the answer of Simeon and Levi stood on that law.
precepts.point: The brothers answered, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot? There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel; the daughters of Israel are not to be handled so, and the sons of Israel did not go for it.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
“There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.”

Jacob was troubled, fearing the nations round about would gather against his house, few in number as it was. The brothers answered him, “Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?” Their answer stood on that law: the daughters of Israel are not to be handled so, and the sons of Israel did not go for it.

precepts.text: When thou shalt vow a vow, thou shalt not slack to pay it, for it would be sin in thee; but if thou forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.
precepts.point: If thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee; but that which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform. Do not suffer thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, and do not say before the angel that it was an error.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
“When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee.” Say a man vows, Lord, if you bring this to pass I will never eat swine again; he must keep that vow. He cannot go back on it and simply ask forgiveness afterward, for the Lord will surely require it of him.

“But if thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.” There is no sin in not vowing at all. The sin is in the mouth that promises and does not perform: “That which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform; even a freewill offering, according as thou hast vowed unto the Lord thy God, which thou hast promised with thy mouth.”

That is Numbers 30 in Moses’ own words again: he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.

precepts.text: Whosoever of Aaron's seed hath any blemish, including him that hath his stones broken, shall not approach to offer the bread of his God.
precepts.point: This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“He that is wounded in the stones, or hath his privy member cut off, shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord.” This law repeats what was already given to the priests. Leviticus lists the blemishes that barred a man of Aaron's seed from approaching to offer the bread of his God: “a blind man, or a lame, or he that hath a flat nose, or any thing superfluous, Or a man that is brokenfooted, or brokenhanded, Or crookbackt, or a dwarf, or that hath a blemish in his eye, or be scurvy, or scabbed, or hath his stones broken”.

The same blemish is in both. “Whosoever he be of thy seed in their generations that hath any blemish, let him not approach to offer the bread of his God”, and among them is he that hath his stones broken; here he that is wounded in the stones shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. What was said of the priest's approach is said again of the congregation.

precepts.text: A bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and the pride of the Philistines shall be cut off.
precepts.point: In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to his tenth generation”. The children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to a place: “And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.”

Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it, and there the bastard dwells. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod; that is the bastard of Ashdod, shut out of the congregation.

precepts.text: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families.
precepts.point: In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families.” Judah's cities are then counted out, “toward the coast of Edom southward”, and the list matters here because Ashdod is in it.

Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance. Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it, and Zechariah says a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. So the city where the bastard dwells, the bastard shut out of the congregation of the Lord, was a city that was Judah's own.

precepts.text: Ashdod with her towns and her villages was among the cities given to Judah.
precepts.point: In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
Among the inheritance of Judah: “Ashdod with her towns and her villages, Gaza with her towns and her villages, unto the river of Egypt, and the great sea, and the border thereof”. Ashdod with her towns and villages was given to the tribe of Judah.

But Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it, and Zechariah says a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. By Nehemiah's day Jews were marrying wives of Ashdod and their children could not speak in the Jews' language: children of forbidden unions with the nations, the bastard shut out of the congregation to the tenth generation, dwelling in a city that was Judah's inheritance.

precepts.text: Jews married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children could not speak in the Jews' language.
precepts.point: In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.”

These are the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations, the bastard the law shuts out of the congregation to his tenth generation, and Ashdod is the very city Zechariah named for the bastard to dwell in, a city given to Judah and lost.

Why did the children speak half in the speech of Ashdod and not the Jews' language? Because the mothers do the raising of the children. A wife of Ashdod raises children that speak Ashdod.

precepts.text: When they read that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.
precepts.point: In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever”. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses: “On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever; Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.”

And when they heard the law, “they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.” Our people had intermarried with the mixed multitude and had children with them, and hearing this law they separated them from Israel. The law still had the same force in Nehemiah's day that it had in Moses': for ever.

precepts.text: Balak king of Moab sent unto Balaam the son of Beor with the rewards of divination to curse Israel, for they were too mighty for him.
precepts.point: Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
The reason Ammon and Moab are shut out for ever: they met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, “and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.” The history is in Numbers.

“And Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites. And Moab was sore afraid of the people, because they were many”. Balak the son of Zippor, king of the Moabites, sent messengers unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, saying, “Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me”. “And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand”. That is the hiring of Balaam.

Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loved thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity all their days for ever.

precepts.text: Tyrus delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and remembered not the brotherly covenant.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”: this was a temporary law, because Edom broke the brotherly covenant. Amos names that covenant: “Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant”.

Tyrus is punished for delivering up the whole captivity to Edom and forgetting the brotherly covenant. The brotherhood this law rests on, he is thy brother, is that covenant, and Edom himself broke it: he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.

precepts.text: Edom did pursue his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever”.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother, was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant: the brother of this law became the one that did pursue his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, his anger tearing perpetually, his wrath kept for ever. And so the punishment of Edom is not turned away.

precepts.text: Edom had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred. He shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity.

As we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. That is why thou shalt not abhor an Edomite was a temporary law: the brother it sheltered kept his wrath for ever.

precepts.text: Egypt shall be a desolation and Edom a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.”

The law says “thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian; because thou wast a stranger in his land.” Many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land. Joel puts Egypt and Edom side by side: both made a desolation, both for the same violence against the children of Judah.

precepts.text: Keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it.
precepts.point: Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing.” When Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing, and the example is Achan.

Before Jericho fell, Israel was warned: “And ye, in any wise keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed, when ye take of the accursed thing, and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it.” That is this law spoken to the host going forth: one wicked thing taken makes the whole camp of Israel a curse and troubles it.

precepts.text: Achan took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
The warning was not kept. “But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.”

Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and though one man took it, the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. When the host went forth and one man did not keep himself from the wicked thing, the whole camp bore it. That is why the law says keep thee from every wicked thing when the host goeth forth.

precepts.text: Israel hath sinned and taken of the accursed thing; therefore they could not stand before their enemies until the accursed was destroyed from among them.
precepts.point: Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
Here is what the wicked thing in the camp cost. “Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff. Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.”

Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them. “There is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel: thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed thing from among you.”

Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant. So when the host goeth forth, keep thee from every wicked thing: it is the wicked thing in the camp that turns the battle.

precepts.text: The law of the uncleanness that chanceth a man by night: he shall wash all his flesh in water and be unclean until the even.
precepts.point: Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
What is the uncleanness that chanceth a man by night? Leviticus gives the law of it: “And if any man’s seed of copulation go out from him, then he shall wash all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the even.”

That is the man of this law. Being unclean until the even, he went abroad out of the camp and did not come within it; when evening came he washed himself with water, as Leviticus commands, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again. The two laws are one: unclean until the even, washed in water, then back in the camp.

precepts.text: Ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and my people shall never be ashamed.
